speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you please tell me how many weeks pregnant you are and describe the severity and location of your abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the abdominal pain feel constant and rigid, rather than coming in intermittent waves like contractions? I also need to know if you have had any recent trauma or if the pain is localized to the site of your previous cesarean scar.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of a previous cesarean section and the sudden onset of severe, constant pain with bleeding, I am highly concerned about uterine rupture. I need to assess the fetal status immediately; can you tell me if you have felt any fetal movement in the last hour, and have you noticed any fluid leaking from your vagina?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: One previous childbirth via cesarean section. No other significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol consumption. Works as an elementary school teacher.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your symptoms of severe pain, bleeding, and a prior cesarean section, I suspect uterine rupture. DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture
